title: Primary and secondary evidence, viewpoint and provenance

questions.prompt: Which source is most clearly a primary account of a council meeting?
choices: The original dated meeting minutes.
A recent textbook summary of the meeting.
A later commentary about the meeting.
questions.explanation: Original contemporaneous minutes are a primary record of the proceedings.

questions.prompt: Which sentence accurately qualifies the authority of a memoir?
choices: Ce témoignage prouve la pensée de chaque habitant.
Tout souvenir personnel est nécessairement exact.
Ce témoignage éclaire une expérience personnelle sans représenter toutes les voix.
questions.explanation: A personal testimony illuminates one perspective without universal representation.

questions.prompt: Which verb best attributes a source's position without endorsing it?
choices: garantit
affirme
démontre définitivement
questions.explanation: Affirme attributes an assertion without asserting that it is proven.

questions.prompt: Choose the construction for citing a newspaper's reported claim.
choices: Selon le journal de l'époque,
En sachant sans source que
Puisque tout le monde pense que
questions.explanation: Selon explicitly identifies the source of a historical claim.

questions.prompt: Which detail belongs in a source-provenance note?
choices: Only the favorite passage of the reader.
Only the number of adjectives in the text.
Date, creator, intended audience and archival reference.
questions.explanation: Date, creator, audience and archive reference support traceability.

questions.prompt: Which phrasing avoids treating one interview as a universal history?
choices: Un seul entretien exclut toute autre perspective.
L'entretien donne accès à une trajectoire parmi d'autres.
L'entretien raconte nécessairement toutes les trajectoires.
questions.explanation: The phrase parmi d'autres explicitly limits representativeness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best description of an editorial's purpose.
choices: Défendre une interprétation auprès d'un public.
Fournir uniquement des mesures sans choix de cadrage.
Remplacer les archives administratives.
questions.explanation: An editorial typically advances an interpretation for an audience.

questions.prompt: Which form marks uncertainty about an archival dating?
choices: Le document a été rédigé sans aucun doute en 1920.
Le document sera certainement rédigé hier.
Le document aurait été rédigé vers 1920.
questions.explanation: Conditional auraient/aurait and vers indicate a tentative date.

questions.prompt: Which sentence appropriately differentiates publication date and event date?
choices: Un texte publié plus tard ne peut évoquer le passé.
Publié en 1980, le récit revient sur les événements de 1955.
Les événements ont forcément eu lieu en 1980.
questions.explanation: Publication year and described event year need not be the same.

questions.prompt: Read « Cette photographie a été légendée trente ans après sa prise. » What is the relevant caution?
choices: The later caption may reflect a different context from the original image.
The camera could not have existed at the original date.
The later caption is automatically fraudulent.
questions.explanation: A caption added decades later may introduce retrospective interpretation.

questions.prompt: Read « La lettre était destinée au préfet, non au grand public. » What can affect its tone?
choices: The letter's paper color alone.
The number of characters in the author's surname.
The intended administrative recipient.
questions.explanation: Audience affects register and what the writer chooses to say.

questions.prompt: Read « L'archive conserve les décisions officielles, mais peu de réactions des riverains. » What limitation is identified?
choices: Proof that nobody lived nearby.
A shortage of residents' perspectives.
A complete absence of official decisions.
questions.explanation: The archive documents authorities more extensively than neighboring residents.

questions.prompt: Read « Ce récit a été traduit du créole vers le français. » What should a critic investigate?
choices: How translation choices may alter nuance or register.
Whether all languages have identical connotations.
Whether translation removes the need for context.
questions.explanation: Translation can change connotation and should be assessed transparently.

questions.prompt: Read « Le document est signé, mais son auteur réel demeure contesté. » What remains uncertain?
choices: Whether a signature appears.
Whether the document has words.
Who actually authored the document.
questions.explanation: A signature exists, but the real author's identity is disputed.

questions.prompt: Read « Deux historiens situent la réforme à des dates différentes. » What should be compared?
choices: Only their academic titles.
Their definitions of the reform and cited evidence.
Only the fonts in their publications.
questions.explanation: Different event boundaries or source evidence may explain conflicting dates.

questions.prompt: Read « L'entretien a été monté pour réduire sa durée. » What is important to know?
choices: Which passages were selected or omitted.
That no original recording could exist.
That editing necessarily falsifies every statement.
questions.explanation: Editing choices can affect emphasis without automatically proving deception.

questions.prompt: Read « Le journal parle de 'progrès' sans expliquer qui en profite. » What question emerges?
choices: Whether the word progrès contains an accent.
How many pages the journal contains.
For whom is the development described as progress?
questions.explanation: The term progrès may privilege a particular group's perspective.

questions.prompt: Read « Une source coloniale décrit la région comme 'vide', tandis que des témoignages évoquent des habitants. » What is the strongest reading?
choices: The witnesses are irrelevant because the archive is official.
The sources make conflicting claims that require contextual scrutiny.
The first source is necessarily comprehensive.
questions.explanation: Conflicting accounts call for attention to perspectives, interests and evidence.

questions.prompt: You cite a wartime leaflet. Which note most improves traceability?
choices: Indicate its date, issuer, archive collection and page or identifier.
Describe the paper as attractive without a citation.
State that the leaflet speaks for an entire population.
questions.explanation: A precise source citation allows others to locate and assess the leaflet.

questions.prompt: You analyze a photograph of a protest. What should you avoid inferring from one image?
choices: That the photograph depicts a visible scene.
That the image was captured from a particular viewpoint.
That every participant shared a single motive.
questions.explanation: One photograph does not establish all participants' intentions.

questions.prompt: You compare a contemporary letter with a memoir written fifty years later. What deserves emphasis?
choices: The assumption that all firsthand texts are identical.
The different times and purposes of each account.
The assumption that later memoirs always tell lies.
questions.explanation: Production timing and genre affect context and interpretation.

questions.prompt: A translated speech omits a culturally specific term. What is a responsible editorial response?
choices: Note the omission and consult the original where possible.
Invent a replacement quotation without attribution.
Assume the omitted term had no meaning.
questions.explanation: Transparency about translation omissions preserves interpretive accountability.

questions.prompt: An official report omits a community's testimony. How do you address the gap?
choices: Write invented testimony to fill the silence.
Declare the community had no views.
Seek additional community sources and explicitly identify the omission.
questions.explanation: Source triangulation and explicit recognition of gaps avoid fabricated evidence.

questions.prompt: You are distinguishing an author's claim from established fact. Which framing fits?
choices: Toutes les sources doivent confirmer cet auteur.
L'auteur soutient que cette réforme fut bénéfique; d'autres sources la contestent.
La réforme fut bénéfique pour tout le monde parce que l'auteur l'affirme.
questions.explanation: Soutient que attributes the argument and acknowledges contesting evidence.

questions.prompt: Two archives disagree about the number of participants. What should you investigate?
choices: Their counting methods, dates and definitions of participation.
The order of letters in each archive's name.
Which archive has the shorter title.
questions.explanation: Disagreement may stem from different definitions, methods or reporting times.

questions.prompt: You must distinguish a reconstruction from direct testimony in a documentary. What label works?
choices: Enregistrement direct d'un événement non filmé.
Témoignage spontané de tous les participants.
Scène reconstituée à partir de sources citées.
questions.explanation: Reconstitution clearly separates dramatization from direct recording.

questions.prompt: A museum label declares a single interpretation settled despite disputed scholarship. What revision is strongest?
choices: Attribuer toutes les interprétations à un seul témoin.
Présenter les principales interprétations et les sources qui les soutiennent.
Supprimer toute référence à l'incertitude historique.
questions.explanation: A fair label presents supported interpretations and their evidentiary limits.
